status: canonical supplemental semantic lineage; preserves all older era forms, modern marks and modern pronunciation rules
warnings: The 24 legacy functions are preserved as contextual readings/lineage, not as 24 new Modern signs.
Secondary meanings require a compatible base or subscript and may not be read as unconditional phoneme insertions.
Do not modify Modern mark shapes, Khmer encodings, glyphs, diacritic placement, or earlier-era artwork.
P remains independent; F = B + Soft Sound + Unvoiced Sound; V = B + Soft Sound.
Separated Vowel requires an actual second vowel subscript on the host.

marks.name: Held Consonant
marks.primary: Lengthens or sustains the host consonant (gemination/held articulation).
marks.secondary: Inherited liquid and stop-coda retention: historical /l/, rolled /r/, /d/, and /t/ can be held or recovered from the host/subscript consonant family.
marks.context: Apply to the actual consonant or subscript being held; it does not insert L, R, D, or T by itself.

marks.name: Central Vowel
marks.primary: Centralizes the host vowel within its letter family.
marks.secondary: Retains the historical Short U /ʌ/ ('uh') reading, now housed in Modern A rather than an independent U.
marks.context: A + Central Vowel gives the former U-family /ʌ/; do not restore an independent Modern U.

marks.name: Open Vowel
marks.primary: Opens or lowers the host vowel quality.
marks.secondary: Unifies the historical open-A contrast: Short A /æ/ and Long A /ɑː/, distinguished by host vowel and Short/Long Vowel as applicable.
marks.context: The open mark denotes vowel quality; duration remains a separate Modern Short/Long Vowel feature.

marks.name: Short Vowel
marks.secondary: Retains the historical short lax front-vowel readings, E /ɛ/ and I /ɪ/, when applied to the corresponding vowel families.
marks.context: Use with E/I-family vowels; it does not independently insert an E or I.

marks.name: Long Vowel
marks.secondary: Consolidates the historical Long E /iː/ and Long U /uː/ readings under one duration mark; vowel identity comes from the host and other marks.
marks.context: Modern /uː/ is hosted by O with Central Vowel + Long Vowel, not independent U.

marks.name: Unvoiced Sound
marks.primary: Devoices an eligible consonant; does not replace its independent base letter.
marks.secondary: Preserves the old voiceless F /f/, S /s/, and K /k/ consonant-class contrasts through Modern base/subscript and voicing recipes.
marks.context: F = B + Soft Sound + Unvoiced Sound. P stays an independent letter; do not read B + Unvoiced Sound as P.

marks.name: Voiced Sound
marks.primary: Adds or preserves voicing on an eligible consonant.
marks.secondary: Retains historical voiced G /g/, B /b/, and Z /z/ readings as contextual consonant-family values, without adding independent Modern letters.
marks.context: B is already /b/ without a mark; historical N+G /ŋ/ belongs to nasal assimilation, not automatic G insertion.

marks.name: Separated Vowel
marks.primary: Maintains hiatus: a host vowel and a genuine second vowel subscript are pronounced as separate nuclei (/V.V/).
marks.secondary: Carries forward the historical Base mark's explicit preservation of an unmodified, individually articulated vowel unit rather than fusing it into a glide.
marks.context: Host-only and valid only when a true second vowel subscript is present; not available on a subscript alone.

marks.name: Nasalization
marks.primary: Adds nasal resonance to the eligible sound.
marks.secondary: Retains the historical M /m/ and N /n/ nasal-coda families as place-dependent nasal readings; /ŋ/ remains possible via contextual nasal assimilation.
marks.context: The mark does not insert arbitrary M/N consonant letters; use their independent/subscript forms when they are pronounced as segments.

marks.name: Soft Sound
marks.primary: Softens or lenites the host consonant; e.g., Modern B + Soft Sound = /v/.
marks.secondary: Retains the historical CH affricate family /tʃ/ and /dʒ/ as a contextual palatal/soft-articulation heritage reading.
marks.context: A CH reading depends on the appropriate T/D-family sound recipe, not Soft Sound alone.

marks.name: Hard Sound
marks.primary: Hardens or fortifies an eligible consonant articulation.
marks.secondary: Retains the historical Hard H family of contextual frication and aspiration (/h/, /θ/, /ʃ/, /ɣ/) where the host consonant calls for it.
marks.context: The same mark's exact IPA depends on the host; it does not turn every consonant into H.

marks.name: Glide Sound
marks.primary: Introduces a family-defined transition glide without an independent extra letter.
marks.secondary: Consolidates the historical W /w/ and Y /j/ semivowel and vowel-glide readings, including inherited diphthong transitions.
marks.context: W and Y remain independent Modern letters when pronounced as full segments; a glide mark is not a substitute for them in every position.
